key_insight: Routine electronic health record data can predict obstructive sleep apnea with moderate accuracy, and a minimal model using age, sex, BMI, and race/ethnicity performed nearly as well as a full-feature model.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support earlier OSA risk flagging inside health systems and may outperform common screening questionnaires like STOP-BANG.
method: Trained tree-ensemble machine learning models on Kaiser Permanente EHR data with sleep-study outcomes.
Compared full 106-feature and minimal 4-feature predictor sets using nested cross-validation.
Validated internally, temporally, and externally at University of Kansas Medical Center, with transfer-learning experiments and comparison to clinical screeners.
evidence_signal: On an internal hold-out set, the full XGBoost model achieved ROC-AUC 0.791 for any OSA and 0.768 for moderate-severe OSA, with external AUCs around 0.69-0.73 and performance above STOP-BANG.
watch_item: External performance dropped versus internal testing, so real-world deployment will need careful calibration, site-specific validation, and attention to data differences across health systems.
paper_title: Machine Learning Models Using Electronic Health Record Data to Predict Obstructive Sleep Apnea
